advisoryTitle: Zod can exhaust memory while validating oversized constrained collections
provenance: Small original v3 adaptation of upstream's early constrained-collection rejection, plus shared parse budgets for v3 issue allocation/traversal across unions/catch/async/native-promise resolution. Schema-field/union-option fanout is reserved before allocating pairs/contexts/promises; exhausted loops stop scheduling and drain already-started async work. Not a verbatim upstream v3 fix or a vendor-fixed package version. Runtime files are emitted from the maintained source with the existing TypeScript compiler.

compatibilityCorpus.runner: Existing Jest with expect/test adapter; unmodified supplier test source and snapshot

intentionalBehaviorChange: Inputs and schema fanout beyond resource limits explicitly fail even if a union/catch could otherwise recover. Missing object fields and union options consume the shared allocation budget before child work; over-wide schemas/unions fail before child contexts. Native-promise results share the original parse budget and reject with ZodError on exhaustion. Async parents observe native-promise validation before accepting/discarding outputs and propagate resource failure, avoiding unhandled rejected child output. Ordinary v3 safeParseAsync rejected-data Promise semantics and original input rejection reasons are retained. Oversized constrained arrays/sets fail before parsing elements. Within-bound valid v3 semantics are retained.
limitations: Not a sandbox for schema-supplied refinements/transforms, getters/proxies, input allocation or unrelated string/regex costs. Map entries reserve two slots. Oversized object-property enumeration can still incur engine enumeration overhead before the bounded loop breaks.
